PR Summary by Qodo

Optimize org tag listing by caching parsed tags and reducing per-paper work ✨ Enhancement 🕐 10-20 Minutes
AI Description

>
>• Cache parsed tag arrays to avoid repeated JSON parsing in org tag listing.
>• Aggregate identical raw tag strings before counting, reducing nested-loop overhead.
>• Micro-optimize hot loops and query normalization to lower CPU and GC pressure.
>
Diagram

```mermaid graph TD A["API Client"] --> B["GET /api/orgs/:slug/tags"] --> C[("D1 DB")] --> D["rawTagCounts (group by tags)"] --> E["parsedTagsCache (Map)"] --> F["parseStoredTags()"] --> G["counts (tag totals)"] --> H["JSON response"] ```
High-Level Assessment

>The following are alternative approaches to this PR:
1. Use an LRU/TTL cache for parsed tags
- ➕ Keeps memory bounded with predictable eviction behavior - ➕ Avoids long-lived cache pollution from one-off tag strings - ➖ More code/complexity than a simple Map - ➖ May add a dependency (or require a small in-house LRU implementation)
2. Request-scoped cache only (no module-level state)
- ➕ No cross-request memory growth - ➕ Eliminates concerns about long-lived process state - ➖ Less reuse across requests, smaller performance gain on hot paths - ➖ Still reparses the same raw tag strings across requests
3. Persist normalized tags at write-time (schema or materialized data)
- ➕ Eliminates JSON parsing from the read path entirely - ➕ Enables more efficient querying/filtering/counting at the database level - ➖ Requires migration/backfill and broader product/data changes - ➖ Higher implementation and rollout risk than a targeted perf fix
>**Recommendation:** The current approach (group identical raw tag strings + module-level parsedTagsCache with a hard cap) is a pragmatic, low-risk performance win for a hot endpoint. If this route remains latency/CPU sensitive, consider upgrading the cache to LRU/TTL to better control memory and keep the hit rate high over time; otherwise, the simple capped Map is an acceptable tradeoff.

2. No-eviction global tags cache 🐞 Bug ☼ Reliability

>Description >

>server-side size/type validation, large or highly-variable tag payloads can make this cache
>disproportionately expensive in long-lived processes.
